reasoning: As of March 19, 2025, the fed funds target range was 4.25%-4.50%, and the FOMC had held rates steady at its January and March meetings. Powell signaled patience because of sticky inflation and uncertainty from tariffs, so the Committee was not signaling imminent cuts. Market pricing at the time expected roughly two cuts in 2025, with the first most likely around June or later. That made a July cut plausible but less likely than a hold, so I put the probability of no change at the July 29-30 meeting somewhat above even. I do not have reliable knowledge of the actual July outcome, so this estimate rests on the March information.
